column4: Visit note | 2025-10-22 10:00 AM | Dr. Selina Parvin, Neurology | Patient: Mala Das, 44, female. Mrs. Das reports experiencing neck tightness and a band-like pressure around her head, linked with long hours at a screen. She works as a shopkeeper and mentions that her symptoms began after a stressful house move to Rangpur. She has no significant medical comorbidities. She denies blurry vision, weakness, or numbness. On examination: pain score 5/10, BP 123/73 mmHg, pulse 69 bpm, weight 66 kg. Cranial nerves are intact and deep tendon reflexes are normal. Assessment: Tension-type headache. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to take screen breaks every hour, perform regular neck stretches, and aim for seven hours of sleep. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-10-22 10:00 AM | Dr. Ishrat Jahan, Psychiatry | Patient: Mostafa Patwary, 27, male. Mr. Patwary attends for review regarding low mood for over three weeks and low energy. He works as a bus driver and states his symptoms began after losing a job in Tangail. He has no chronic medical comorbidity. He denies sleep disturbance of an organic cause or substance misuse. On examination: PHQ-9 score 10, BP 114/73 mmHg, pulse 74 bpm, weight 71 kg. He appears cooperative and oriented. Assessment: Depressive episode. Plan: a prescription was issued. The patient denies thoughts of self-harm, and a safety plan with the emergency number 999 was discussed. He was advised to keep a daily routine, walk outdoors daily, start counselling sessions, and call 999 or come to the clinic at once if thoughts of self-harm appear. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-10-22 10:30 AM | Dr. Kamrul Hasan, Pulmonology | Patient: Habiba Awal, 63, female. Mrs. Awal attends for review of wheezing on walking and a long history of smoking. She works as a shopkeeper and notes her symptoms flared after rubbish was burned near her home in Mirpur. She has a known comorbidity of Bronchial asthma. She denies fever or chest pain. On examination: SpO2 87%, BP 119/80 mmHg, pulse 89 bpm, weight 60 kg. Auscultation reveals widespread expiratory wheeze. Assessment: COPD exacerbation. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to stop smoking completely, avoid cooking smoke, and take the yearly flu vaccine. Follow-up in 1 week, sooner if breathing worsens.
